assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last year's performer laminate press PDF, exactly as the printer returned it (single record, one representative pass on one page; to be reverse-engineered into a live merge template downstream).

Document: single PORTRAIT laminate, 100 x 140 mm, one pass on the page, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the shape the printer runs the whole roster on; the client wants the same shape this year in the NEW palette with new names.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (five apparent blocks, top to bottom):
- PHOTO BOX: a portrait rectangle across the top for a headshot, filled Old Pine with a thin cream keyline and a faint diagonal cross.
- NAME BLOCK: the person's name, large, in a bold condensed display face.
- ACT LINE: the act, one line under the name, in the condensed face at a smaller size.
- ROLE BAR: a full-width coloured bar with the ROLE word reversed out in cream, colour-coded so gate staff read it at distance.
- STAGE & DAY STRIP: a small two-line strip at the foot, 'Stages: ...' then 'Days: ...' in a plain grotesque.
There is also a small SOCIAL HANDLE line between the act line and the role bar, set in a low-contrast pale tint that sits close in value to the Old Pine ground.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The NAME, the ACT LINE, the SOCIAL HANDLE, the ROLE word and the STAGE & DAY text are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame that flows top-to-bottom beneath the photo box, NOT five addressable per-field frames. The role bar's coloured background is a separate drawn rectangle sitting behind the role word; the role word itself lives inside the one flowing story.
- The PHOTO BOX is a DRAWN filled rectangle plus keyline and cross (grouped vector paths), NOT a rectangular picture/graphic frame. There is NO image well anywhere on the pass even though the box reads like one, so a per-performer headshot from the roster's Headshot column has no graphic frame to bind into.
- The mapping readout used to build offsets is LOSSY: it silently omits the low-contrast SOCIAL HANDLE run (it sits close in value to its ground) while KEEPING that run's line break, so the reconstructed string still looks well-formed and every offset AFTER the handle (ROLE, STAGES, DAYS) is short by exactly that run. The validator still answers VALID with no warnings and prepare still answers completed successfully; only a placeholder inventory read back out of the prepared document reveals that ROLE, STAGES and DAYS never landed on the run they were meant to.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content in the story, not as visible tokens): NAME | ACT | HANDLE | ROLE | STAGES | DAYS

COLOURS (LAST YEAR's palette, carried in this file; this year uses the new brand palette): ground Old Pine #223A34, name and role-word cream Bone-Old #EAE0C8, role bar Faded Teal #2E5A63, the low-contrast social-handle line Shade Pine #34473F (close to the ground). New palette to swap in this year: Night Field #1B2A2E, Lantern Amber #E8A13A, Ember Red #C24634, Meadow #6E8B5B, Bone #F2EAD9, Dusk Ink #12181B.

FONTS (embedded, last year's): display 'Fairgrove Condensed' Bold for the name and act, grotesque 'Halyard Grotesk' Regular/Medium for the handle and the stage & day strip.

assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot at a slight upward angle, of a large weathered hand-painted CANVAS banner lashed across the top of an outdoor wooden festival main stage at dusk, a fictional folk festival, no real logos or trademarks. Painted on the pale oatmeal canvas in one deep charcoal-green ink is a compound festival MARK: a simple lantern seen face-on with three small cut window panes glowing, and around the lantern a RING of small-caps hand-lettered type reading 'LANTERNWOOD FOLK FEST', with a single hand-painted rule sweeping beneath. The window panes and the little counters inside the ring letters are painted with THIN brush strokes and tight small openings. Uneven natural side light so the LEFT and centre of the banner are clearly lit but the RIGHT THIRD falls into soft shade where the charcoal-green painted ink and the aged oatmeal canvas run close together in value and the edges of the paint go soft. Visible canvas weave, faint sag and wind creases, a couple of old paint chips, casual real-world snapshot look, not a studio shot, no people.

assets.prompt: A flatbed scan of a site manager's HAND-DRAWN pencil site plan on a slightly creased sheet of off-white paper, drawn in graphite with a ruler and freehand, for a fictional three-stage folk festival on a farm field. Drawn features, loosely hand-lettered in pencil: a large MAIN FIELD STAGE at the top of the field, a smaller MEADOW STAGE at left, a BARN STAGE at right, a GATES / ENTRY at the bottom, a FOOD ROW along one edge, a CAMPING block, a FIRST AID tent, toilets, and a dashed ACCESSIBLE ROUTE line winding from the gates to the main field. A rough north arrow and a couple of smudges and eraser marks. Pure pencil-on-paper scan, no colour, no computer type, no logos, casual and clearly hand-made.
